summary: SL-107 was the hand-off for SL-089's last unmet criterion, the person's whole-C:\ W-001 run. It shipped docs/design/SL-107-c-drive-run.md, two sentences in SL-089-seams.md, a counts-only fitness rule over the future c-drive-run.json with a 44-row corpus, bounded-root cases C-001..C-006, and an unplanned change to eng/rules-harness (awaiting_file, a plant-over-existing-record path, rows S83-S86/P36). The run and the record still do not exist, so SL-089 criterion 3 is as unmet as when SL-107 was filed. The design said "change no code" and the builder had to edit shared harness tooling, which skipped the critique and drove most of the 4 code reviews.

It shipped docs/design/SL-107-c-drive-run.md, two sentences in SL-089-seams.md, a counts-only fitness rule over the future c-drive-run.json with a 44-row corpus, bounded-root cases C-001..C-006, and an unplanned change to eng/rules-harness (awaiting_file, a plant-over-existing-record path, rows S83-S86/P36). The run and the record still do not exist, so SL-089 criterion 3 is as unmet as when SL-107 was filed. The design said "change no code" and the builder had to edit shared harness tooling, which skipped the critique and drove most of the 4 code reviews.
payload.estimate_error: Risk tier medium held: nothing shipped to users broke, and Test-W001 was not touched, so Q-114's 6-minute WindowMutants run was avoided. The size was under-called. The design said "docs only, no code", but the build changed eng/rules-harness/harness.py and plants.json (15 files over 2 builds). That tooling gates every later slice that touches fitness.yaml (Q-027), so that part was medium-high risk and unplanned. The effort followed it: design 2 laps, critique 2, build 2, code review 4 (2 halted), plus 2 failed checks at validate. Lesson #425's "record plus recipe" sizing predicted a light review load for a docs and tests slice. It did not predict the load when a fitness rule is added over a file that does not exist yet.

learned.lesson: An architecture rule over a file the slice does not create (here .taad/slices/SL-089/c-drive-run.json, which only the person's run writes) is the most expensive part of an otherwise docs-only slice. The repo's own rules harness refuses a clean baseline with an unmatched rule (exit 2). Q-012 says every engine gate treats pass-with-unmatched as a pass, but it does not describe this harness. The cost was awaiting_file in plants.json, load_awaiting at harness.py:699, the overwrite path in Planting._create (harness.py:399-405), plant rows S83-S86 and P36, and a stand-alone Python pin. A later slice that wants a rule over a to-be-created file should budget that in the design, or leave the rule out and rely on the writer's write-time allow-list.
learned.evidence: build-slice #1 'one unplanned fix was needed'; code-review #1 M1; build-slice #2 O-016; plants.json:248-252; code-review #3 R3-m1 (awaiting_file must stay while any row plants the record, and SC-347 is waived to the backlog).

learned.lesson: When a 'change no code' design makes the builder edit shared infra, the edit skips the critique. It enters at build, after critique, and only code review sees it. Here that was eng/rules-harness (gated by Q-027), and the code reviews ran 4 times. A builder who finds the design's no-code premise false should send the slice back to design rather than patch and carry on. The same applies to WindowCases.ps1, which Q-114 gates.
learned.evidence: Critique #1 and #2 ran on a design with no harness change. The harness change first appears in build-slice #1; code-review #1 M1, code-review #3 R3-m1 and the C-008 bite all came from it.

learned.lesson: An obligation whose builder instruction is to hand-edit .taad/slices/<id>/design-slice-N.json cannot be discharged. Q-106 already answered that the file is an engine export that the next refresh overwrites. In SL-107 the refresh reverted would_force_resynthesis and the rule patterns, and build #2 then committed the re-exported file. Both code-review #1 and #3 logged it as drift, and validate failed a check on it. O-002/O-015 should have been discharged by a disposition or a doc sentence, not an edit to the export. Check Q-106 before writing such an instruction.
learned.evidence: code-review #1 'engine's export refresh has already reverted the builder's edits'; code-review #3 'O-015 is not true of the tree'; validate-slice failed check 'committed design record agrees with O-015's account'.

learned.lesson: A person-run criterion needs the up-front checked_by: person marking from lesson #357, and the build-check must obey it. Build-check #2's model decision said 'build makes the run itself, unattended', citing Q-176. Design #1 then halted on an open question, and design #2 reversed it. The settled reading is that Q-176's unattended-W-001 allowance does not extend to -Root C:\. Pool growth the kernel keeps until a restart (#348: predicted 3-4.4 GiB for a cold exe scan) would hold every engine agent. Neither the 0.5 GB nor the 3 GB figure changes that.
learned.evidence: build-check #2 decision text vs design-slice #2 decision and O-002's disposition.

learned.lesson: The deliverable is still absent after SL-089 and SL-107, and nothing in the loop prompts a person to make it. Q-107/Q-108 say nothing schedules or reminds, and there is no person-owed queue. SC-136/SC-138 (backlog checks by hand) are the only holders. Do not build more tooling around the whole-C:\ run until a first real record exists. The unknowns that only that record answers are TIMEOUT at 1,200 s, the real Layers share of the old 682, and whether the path rule and awaiting_file hold on a real committed file.
learned.evidence: validate-slice 'not reached' list: deliverable, same-session anchors, TIMEOUT ending, real-record path-rule check. Q-107/Q-108 answers.

learned.lesson: The 682-684 expected counts (652 code 5 / 28 code 363 / 2 code 1920) cannot be reproduced by the run the slice specifies. They came from scans that entered Containers\Layers (U-112 groups of 10, 8 and 7 rows under Layers). With the wcifs precaution on, the store is notScanned 1. The spike path lists are gone (no a-c-drive.json, C.rows.tsv or misses.tsv under %TEMP%\taad3-runs). So criterion 5 is judged against same-session anchor runs (C:\Windows, C:\ProgramData, %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp) and Q-261's ceilings, not against 682. The code-363 count is compared to that day's Temp anchor, because new cloud cases add stuck placeholders (#360).
learned.evidence: critique M2 and O-012 (floor by anchors); Q-261; spike w001-other-code-row-checks (stand-in-bin folders are no longer reparse points, so 1920 is expected 0-2).

learned.lesson: Get-OracleRow sends a code-1920 NothingListed row to 'other-code', and so to notARefusedKeepShape. It does not go to leftoverRows. SC-136's '~30 leftover rows' (28 code 363 + 2 code 1920) was therefore the wrong expectation. Expect oracle.leftoverRows.code363 27-28, leftoverRows.reparse 0, and 1920 rows (0-2) only under notARefusedKeepShape. The corpus rows F02 (leak) and F12 (1920 = other-code) pin this.
learned.evidence: WindowCases.ps1 Get-OracleRow 6132-6145; W001OracleCorpus.json F12; validate-slice oracle test 21/21.

learned.lesson: Lesson #174's 1,299 s whole-C: figure and its 'hook deadline is 120 s' warning are stale for W-001. Rows mode has no deadline (RowsMode.cs:18; the 120 s is TreeMode.cs:73), and Test-W001 waits 1,200 s (WindowCases.ps1:6220). Whole-C: Core scans since SL-056 took 159-409 s (U-108, U-110, U-111). The cold app rate projects to about 468 s (C:\Windows 71.8 s for 157,709 folders). Validate still quoted 400-1,600 s with #174, so a TIMEOUT is possible but not expected. If it happens, raise the 1,200 literal and run WindowMutants -Mutant All (Q-114).
learned.evidence: risk-spike app-scan-rate-fits-1200s-timeout; validate-slice 'TIMEOUT ending' left-open entry; design key decision 1.

learned.lesson: RuleCases cases are bounded by the engine's 120 s repro limit (Q-222, repro.py:63). C-008 sits at about 80 s, and adding a mutation bite took it to 127 s. A new pin for rules-harness behaviour belongs in a stand-alone tests/bugs script (the Python pin runs in 0.3 s), not in RuleCases. Do not extend C-007/C-008-class cases without measuring headroom first.
learned.evidence: build-slice #2: 'a RuleCases bite took C-008 to 127 s... removed; C-008 is back to 80 s'.

learned.lesson: Any hand-off or case that tees a native child's output through pwsh to keep a path must set [Console]::OutputEncoding to UTF-8 first. This PC's OEM code page is 437, and a CJK or accented letter in a LEAK path became '?' or a lookalike, in the file and on screen. Tee-Object also does not create a missing parent folder, and the main checkout on uat has no artifacts\ until a build runs. Both are now in the SL-107 doc. Reuse the pattern for later person-run captures.
learned.evidence: code-review #1 round 2 (R2-m2, simulated at code page 437); critique M1 and O-011 (measured 'Could not find a part of the path').

lessons_judged.why: Criteria 1-5 were kept checked_by person and no machine case waits on the run. Design #2 and O-002 refused any engine run of -Root C:\ on that basis. Build-check #2's decision to run it in the engine went against this lesson and was reversed.

The doc uses -Root C:\ from pwsh and warns that cmd.exe delivers C:". Case C-001 proves it arrives as C:" and exits 1 with no record. The design relied on Format-AppArgument's trailing-backslash doubling for the app.
Test-W001's oracle was left alone. Corpus rows F02 (leak) and F12 (1920 = other-code) pin the classification the doc's endings table describes, and the doc says a leak's fix starts with the corpus.
It drove the move from a fixed 27-28 code-363 range to 'equal to the same-session Temp anchor'. New cloud-case leftovers become 363 rows in later C: scans.
The design subtracts the fsa-guard-tests, fsa-window-cases and fsa-validate-2 fixtures in the reconciliation table instead of cleaning them first (Q-258 wants them kept).
It set the expectation that the 27 code-363 rows are CreateFile failures (byKind.openedNothingListed 0, oracle.opened 0). C-006 confirmed this, and no Sandbox runs were spent re-measuring 363.
All builds and runs went through eng/dotnet.ps1. The risk spikes had to copy the repo-local .dotnet into a scratch worktree because the host has no .NET 10 SDK.

Its 1,299 s whole-C: scan predates SL-056, and whole-C: Core scans now take 159-409 s. Its '120 s ending deadline' is TreeMode's; W-001's rows mode has none and waits 1,200 s. Validate still quoted the stale figure.
The slice was designed as record plus recipe with no default-suite Facts. Its limit showed: review load still scaled with the unplanned harness change, 4 code reviews against a docs-only surface.
The doc's pre-flight warns that a cold scan may cost several GiB of kernel pool. O-002's reason for keeping the run out of the engine rests on the 3-4.4 GiB prediction.
Criterion 5 is a whole-drive count comparison, so churn tolerance was defined up front: ceilings, anchors and named fixture rows, not strict equality with 682.
Every build, test, publish and W-001 run in this slice went through eng/dotnet.ps1, and the worktree downloaded its own .dotnet.
Cases C-004..C-006 ran WindowCases.ps1 directly. dotnet test never runs window cases, so the default suite (964/964) said nothing about the whole-drive branch.

The rule was added as a settled entry with plant rows and verified with rules-parity and the harness. The 'move above the marker, add an xUnit Fact' part was not needed for a settled rule (parity: AGREE, 73 settled). The lesson does not cover a rule over a not-yet-existing file.

'Any rule edit must change both files' (yaml and ArchitectureRulesTests.cs) did not hold. SL-107 appended a settled rule changing only fitness.yaml (plus harness rows), and rules-parity still printed AGREE. The '8 entries' figure is stale too: Fitness now reads 95 rules.

what_went_wrong: The design said 'change no code', but build #1 had to edit eng/rules-harness/harness.py and plants.json. The repo's harness exits 2 on a clean baseline that contains an unmatched rule, which Q-012's 'gates treat it as a pass' does not cover. That edit entered after the critique, so only code review saw it. The cascade was M1 (five plant rows PLANT-BROKEN once the record exists), the Planting overwrite path in build #2, a RuleCases bite that took C-008 to 127 s past the 120 s limit and was reverted, a new Python pin, and R3-m1 (the builder's follow-up said awaiting_file 'can be dropped', which is false).

O-002/O-015 told the build to hand-edit .taad/slices/SL-107/design-slice-1.json. Q-106 had already answered that the file is an engine export. The refresh reverted would_force_resynthesis and the patterns, build #2 committed the re-exported file, and O-015 was recorded 'discharged' while the tree says otherwise. Code review #1 and #3 and validate each re-found it.

Code review ran 4 times and halted twice (#1 on M1, #3 on a false follow-up plus drift that no file edit could fix). Validate passed with two failed checks filed as extras: the doc's code-363 rule replaces Q-261's answered 27-28 range, and the design record's drift.

Build-check #2 decided that the engine would make the whole-C:\ run itself, against lesson #357. Design #1 halted on an open question, a model answered it (Q-261), and design #2 reversed the build-check decision. One halted design lap and one decision were spent on whether the engine may run the scan.

All critique and code-review dispositions after the first were answered by a model while the owner was away. The gate counts them as untriaged, and the Q-261 override of an answered number went through that way.

The slice's stated purpose is unmet. SL-089 criterion 3 and all five derived criteria are still 'not reached: a person's to run', and no record exists on any branch. The only things holding it are the SC-136/SC-138 checks by hand.

missed.what: The design claimed the appended counts-only rule 'matches no file until the person commits it, and the gates treat that as a pass (Q-012)', and that no code changes. It never asked which repo-level consumers read Fitness's unmatched list. The repo's rules harness (eng/rules-harness/harness.py check_clean and describe_unmatched) refuses a clean baseline with an unmatched rule (exit 2), and RuleCases C-007 asserts 'none unmatched'. A check was owed: run harness.py clean baseline on a tree with the rule and no record.
missed.caught_by: build-slice #1 (the builder hit exit 2 and added awaiting_file)

missed.what: The design's capture command rested on a recalled claim that Tee-Object streams a native child's stdout. Critique M1 checked the missing artifacts\ folder but not the decoding. The parent pwsh decodes the child's output with [Console]::OutputEncoding, which is OEM 437 on this PC. A LEAK path with non-OEM characters, the capture's only purpose, came out as '?' or a lookalike, in the file and on screen. A check was owed: pipe a child that prints U+4E2D and U+0151 through the command at the default code page.

The m3 disposition ('in the design record, set would_force_resynthesis to false') and the O-002/O-015 builder instruction ordered a hand-edit of an engine-exported design-slice-1.json. Q-106 already says those files are overwritten on refresh. The edit was reverted and the obligation was recorded discharged against a tree that disagrees.

The M2 disposition replaced Q-261's answered, decided 27-28 code-363 range with 'equal to the same-session Temp anchor' without reopening Q-261 or noting the override on it. The critique should have flagged that an accepted fix overrides an answered question. The two rules agree today (27 + 1 = 28).

Critique m2 asked for a check that the rule fires and stays quiet on a record. The disposition did not say how to run it against the real path, .taad/slices/SL-089/c-drive-run.json, without colliding with the file the person will commit. The builder implemented it as new-file plant rows at that path. The critique should have asked what happens to those rows once the record exists.

unknowns: Does the whole-C:\ rows-mode run finish inside Test-W001's 1,200 s wait on this PC today? The spike projects about 468 s cold, whole-C: Core scans took 159-409 s, and lesson #174's 1,299 s is a pre-SL-056 figure. A TIMEOUT writes no record, and the fix is raising the literal at WindowCases.ps1:6220 plus a WindowMutants run (Q-114).

When the person's record exists, does Q-261's reconciliation hold? That means notScanned 1, code 363 equal to that day's Temp anchor (27-28 at bd6572f), code 1920 at 0-2, Unreadable at most 682, and rows at least the sum of the C:\Windows, C:\ProgramData and Temp anchors. The Layers share of the old 682 is unmeasurable because the spike path lists are gone, so a shortfall cannot be told apart from an under-count.

Does the committed real record keep the counts-only rule quiet, and does the awaiting_file overwrite in harness.py Planting._create hold with the real file present? Only P36 (a bounded-run record) and the 44-row corpus stand in. The full harness run has only been done with no record at the path.
Does the person ever run it? Nothing schedules or reminds (Q-107/Q-108). SC-136/SC-138 are the only holders, and the record, if made, lands on whichever checkout runs the script.

candidates.title: Give the harness's plant-over-record pin a routine runner
candidates.why: tests/bugs/SL-107-HarnessPlantsOverRecord.Tests.py (4 tests, 0.3 s under the engine venv) is the only thing that fails if the awaiting_file overwrite branch in eng/rules-harness/harness.py Planting._create (lines ~399-405) is removed. Until the person commits .taad/slices/SL-089/c-drive-run.json, the five rows S83, S84, S85, S86 and P36 (plants.json:248-252) run in create mode and pass either way. A regression would then show only at the Q-027 full-harness validate of an unrelated later slice, which fails with PLANT-BROKEN once the record exists. Code reviews #3 and #4 recorded that no routine gate runs the test. Q-253 says catalog rows re-run at every validate, but shippability.append refuses commands not measured red. RuleCases C-008 has no headroom (80 s, and a bite took it to 127 s against the 120 s limit). The fix is to make harness.py --scenario all, or another routine gate, call the pin.
